prompt_en: An investigative-fiction photograph of a human investigator examining physical evidence at an archive loading dock. A separate archive clerk has stopped a low platform trolley beside the open bay; the investigator is documenting a severed security seal before the transport crate moves farther inside. Use the supplied portrait as the visible face and hair appearance reference for the investigator, preserving the rounded face, dark brown eyes and chin-length dark bob with a wispy fringe. Her quiet, attractive presence comes through a composed profile, soft light on her cheek and absorbed attention to the damaged fastening. She wears an ordinary fitted charcoal work jacket and straight trousers. The crate's broad front face turns toward the viewer. A flat orange security band crosses its central metal latch and has been severed in one place: two squared free ends remain attached on opposite sides of a clearly exposed interval of bare dark crate face. The severed security seal has two visibly separate cut ends with an open gap between them. The band is broad enough and the six-centimetre gap is large enough to read in this full scene; both ends lie flat in the same front plane. The two free tips turn outward away from opposite sides of the hasp within the front plane, centering the clear bare patch between their severed edges. The investigator photographs and measures the severed security seal, directing the camera in her right hand and the measuring scale in her left hand at that same seal. Her right fingers close around the camera grip, with its lens aimed at the exposed gap; her left fingers hold the end of a rigid metric scale against the crate face directly below it. The measuring scale touches the crate beside the seal while its marked edge spans the two cut ends. She hinges slightly from the hips with her elbows separated, keeping the scale and camera on different visible sightlines. The depicted camera lens sits just above the measuring edge and faces the gap from that higher position; the scale edge runs parallel to the interval between the tips. Her gaze follows the camera's screen toward the same target. The separate clerk waits with both hands gripping the trolley handle. The handle stands clear of the crate, with each of the clerk's wrists, fingers and contact patches visible. The entire crate base rests on the trolley platform, the platform connects to the wheels, and the wheels meet the floor. Both people have both feet visibly planted on the loading-dock floor. A strip of floor extends beyond every shoe and wheel. The crate is centered on a slightly larger open platform, with its four small casters staggered in projection so each wheel-floor contact can be seen. Make one horizontal full-length photograph from a gently elevated front three-quarter position, placing the investigator at the left, the sealed crate in the middle and the waiting clerk to the right. Keep both complete figures, every support endpoint and the seal together within the frame, with generous lower-edge breathing room. The crate occupies enough frame width for the cut ends, ruler markings and directed camera lens to remain distinct. Soft daylight from the open bay grazes the orange ends against the dark crate face; quiet interior shelving supplies the archival setting. Soft daylight reflected from the pale dock floor separates the charcoal jacket and trouser outlines from the shelving behind the investigator. Moderate depth of field keeps the face, hands, seal, trolley and floor contacts clear together. The image feels like a precise pause in real work, with the discovered interruption and the held transport route connected in one readable moment.
